diagnostics.message: The explicit depends_on from :resource.local_file.public_ssh_key to :resource.tls_private_key.ssh duplicates the ordinary reference to tls_private_key.ssh in the content attribute.
The explicit depends_on from :resource.local_file.private_ssh_key to :resource.tls_private_key.ssh duplicates the ordinary reference to tls_private_key.ssh in the content attribute.

The explicit depends_on from :resource.null_resource.file_permission to :resource.local_file.private_ssh_key duplicates the dependency needed by the provisioner command: the private key file resource produces the file whose permissions are changed.

The Auto Scaling group can launch the runner agent before its inline CloudWatch Logs role policy is installed. Because logging is enabled by default and the instance user data configures logging, wait for this policy before creating the group.

The Auto Scaling group may launch the runner agent before its IAM role policy attachment granting docker-machine permissions is installed. The group should wait for the attachment so the agent can use those permissions as soon as it starts.

When service-linked-role creation is enabled, the runner agent needs this policy attachment before it starts using its instance role; otherwise its initial operations can race the attachment and fail to create service-linked roles.
The runner's user-data logging configuration may start before the managed CloudWatch log group exists. Ensure the group is created before the Auto Scaling group launches the runner instance.

When token management is enabled, runner user data uses SSM to manage the registration token. The Auto Scaling group should wait for this role-policy attachment so the instance has the required SSM permissions when it starts.
The runner instance role needs the cache policy attachment before the runner can use the configured S3 cache. Ensure the attachment is in place before the Auto Scaling group launches an instance.
The runner's user-data flow manages the registration token in this SSM parameter. Waiting for the parameter to exist avoids the instance attempting to write it before Terraform has created it.

The runner agent can start provisioning Docker-machine instances as soon as it boots, but this Docker-machine security-group ingress rule may not yet be installed. Ensure the rule exists before launching the agent.
The runner agent can start provisioning Docker-machine instances as soon as it boots, but this SSH ingress rule may not yet be installed. Ensure the rule exists before launching the agent.
The runner agent can start provisioning Docker-machine instances as soon as it boots, but this Docker-machine egress rule may not yet be installed. Ensure the rule exists before launching the agent.
